Every year, inadequate cold chains waste 526 million tonnes of food, enough to feed 950 million people. Farmers lose around 15% of their income because they cannot access higher-value markets.
 
How much value are we leaving on the table?
 
The answer depends on one critical factor: energy.
 
It was a pleasure to join the Permanent Mission of Malaysia and CPOPC at the HLPF 2026 side event on Powering Green Growth: Inclusive Solutions for Energy and Industry through Agro-Value Chains.
 
Nearly 30% of global energy is used by agri-food systems, and more than 70% of that energy is consumed after food leaves the farm in cooling, processing, transport, and logistics. This is where countries capture value, build competitive industries, and create better jobs.
 
The real opportunity is not producing more. It is producing more value. Clean energy enables higher-value processing, stronger cold chains, digital and AI-enabled services, and the next generation of green jobs. Already 375 million people work in off-farm agri-food activities, and as agricultural production grows by 14% over the next decade, geospatial intelligence can help direct investment where renewable energy creates the greatest economic impact.
 
At UNDP, we are helping make that happen. In Nepal, our first agrovoltaic farming system supports more than 450 households with renewable energy, irrigation, and higher-value agriculture. In Kenya, our partnership with UNCDF is expected to mobilize US$31 million for solar cold storage, strengthening local value chains and reducing post-harvest losses.
 
Green growth is ultimately about turning clean energy into productive capital, connecting renewable energy with agriculture, finance and local enterprise so countries create more value at home rather than exporting it abroad.
 
Thank you to the Permanent Missions of Malaysia and Indonesia, CPOPC and fellow panelists for an excellent discussion.
